newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: United NZ leader balks at coalition with ACT.
newsitem.headline: United NZ leader balks at coalition with ACT.

text.p: United New Zealand leader Clive Matthewson on Wednesday all but ruled out joining a coalition which included the radical free market ACT New Zealand Party.
United's seven MPs were National's coalition partners in the run up to the October 12 election, but on current polling the party is set to win only one or two seats.

"We have always said we could form a coalition with National and Labour, but that doesn't extend to others Labour may join, so it doesn't necessarily extend to National's either," Matthewson told Reuters.
"So perhaps we would not join a coalition with ACT in it. In fact I would put it stronger and say very likely not."

ACT and the Christian Coalition are averaging about five percent in the polls. Unless National forges a deal with one of the three opposition parties it will need to look to one or both of the two for support to form a government.

Matthewson and United's only cabinet minister, Internal Affairs Minister Peter Dunne, had earlier warned of what they said would be "extremist" policies if ACT exerted an influence on the ruling conservative National Party.

Matthewson said ACT would have a "malignant influence" on National, while Dunne said "a National-led government beholden to ACT is just as bad as a Labour-led government beholden to the (left wing) Alliance".
"Either we could join a coalition and pull in a different direction (from ACT) or we could say we won't join but will vote to continue sensible polices," Matthewson said.
He said United did not have the same reservations about National's other potential coalition partner, the Christian Coalition.

However, he said the centrist Christian Democrats would be easier to work with, and United may "find problems with some of the ideas" of the more morally conservative Christian Heritage. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473 4746
